question: What brings about determination, and why can it not be forced otherwise?
premises: A particular aspect may be about to manifest.
Determination occurs when that particular aspect settles.
This settling follows the inclination of the knowing subject and not mere passage of time.
inference: Determination depends on the subject's oriented settling of a particular, not on time alone.
uncertainties: Mātṛruci may imply interest, readiness, or cognitive orientation; the verse leaves it broad.
plain_english: When the particular aspect that is about to manifest settles, determination arises; it arises according to the inclination of the knowing subject, and not otherwise, not even after countless ages.
